agent_summary:
Lane: Business logic (WSTG-BUSL) against juice.lab.test (OWASP Juice Shop, http only; read-only engagement, no test accounts, writes disallowed). ~120 read-only requests across the real API/file surface.

DONE (evidence attached):
- BUSL-01 Data validation: /rest/products/search q param is concatenated into SQL — UNION payload returned SQLite version 3.44.2 in the id field (x32) and q=' OR 1=1-- returns a 500 SQL stack trace (x85); /rest/track-order accepts arbitrary unvalidated order-ID strings (template/format/command/SSI payloads all return normal 200, x83/x84/x71/x72).
- BUSL-02 Forge requests: /rest/track-order/{1,5,7,8} return order data with no session (IDOR, x12/x16/x113/x119); substring-allowlist open redirect confirmed (/redirect?to=https://evil.example.com/?x=<allowlisted> → 302, x54; plain external rejected 406, x55). Lead recorded on likely registration mass-assignment (POST /api/Users, not exercised — needs write).
- BUSL-03 Integrity: deluxe membership eligibility enforced server-side (x17, positive); campaign coupon code list recoverable from /ftp (x44) undermining discount integrity. Basket/checkout price tampering not testable read-only.
- BUSL-05 Function-use limits: feedback CAPTCHA /rest/captcha is unauthenticated and returns its own answer (x6), so the anti-automation control is trivially bypassable; image-captcha requires login (x8); per-product limitPerUser exists (x13).
- BUSL-06 Workflow circumvention: order tracking reachable unauthenticated by ID (x16) while admin order-history is blocked 403 (x30) — inconsistent route protection.
- BUSL-07 Misuse defenses: app blocks some abuse (403 "Malicious activity detected" on single Quantitys records and admin routes; 500 "Blocked illegal activity by <IP>" on unauth order-history, x14/x15/x30/x50) but leaks internal stack traces/paths, allows account enumeration via /rest/user/security-question (real email → question, unknown → {}, x25/x29), and shows no rate limiting against repeated probing. CORS is wildcard but a spoofed Origin was not reflected (x53), so no credentialed-CORS.

OPEN (could not be tested read-only):
- BUSL-04 Process timing: timing side-channels (login/reset) need POST and precise timing unavailable through the rate-limited gateway; only a content-based account oracle was observed (noted on item).
- BUSL-08 Upload of unexpected file types: /file-upload is POST-only (OPTIONS x36) and writes are disallowed; as related read-only evidence the /ftp file server's .md/.pdf extension allowlist is bypassable via poison null byte (x62/x63/x64/x79/x81/x82/x98), showing broken extension validation.
- BUSL-09 Upload of malicious files (XXE/zip-slip): requires authenticated POST to /file-upload; not exercised.

Additional leads recorded for reviewer: feedback CAPTCHA answer disclosure (medium), unauthenticated order-tracking IDOR (medium), /api/Recycles/{id} object-level authz gap (Recycles/1-4 return records unauthenticated while collection is "not supported", x101/x102/x106/x118, medium), potential user-registration mass-assignment (high, needs write). Also confirmed other lanes' findings in passing: /rest/memories exposes redacted password/token/email (x59), /metrics and /support/logs and /ftp + /ftp/quarantine directory listings reachable unauthenticated. Note: /.env, /sitemap.xml, /crossdomain.xml, /clientaccesspolicy.xml just return the SPA index (catch-all), i.e. not real exposed files.

leads.title: [agent] Feedback CAPTCHA answer disclosed in its own response (defeats anti-automation limit)

detail.text: GET /rest/captcha (unauthenticated) returns JSON containing both the challenge and the correct answer, e.g. {"captchaId":0,"captcha":"8-4-4","answer":"0"}. Because the answer is handed to the client, the CAPTCHA that is supposed to limit automated feedback/review submission can be solved programmatically and reused indefinitely, so there is no effective per-function usage limit on feedback. The stronger /rest/image-captcha requires login (401).

leads.title: [agent] Order tracking allows unauthenticated access to arbitrary order IDs

detail.text: GET /rest/track-order/1 and /rest/track-order/5 return order data with no session/Authorization header (200, {"status":"success","data":[{"orderId":"..."}]}). An anonymous user can enumerate and read any order's tracking record by ID, bypassing the account/checkout workflow. Compare with admin route /rest/order-history/orders which is correctly blocked (403 "Malicious activity detected").

leads.title: [agent] Potential mass-assignment of privileged fields on user registration (needs write to confirm)

detail.text: GET /api/Users requires auth (401) but the collection supports POST (registration) per OPTIONS (GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE, wildcard CORS). In OWASP Juice Shop the registration endpoint accepts an extra "role":"admin" field, allowing self-registration of an admin account. This could not be exercised because the engagement is read-only; a reviewer should verify whether POST /api/Users accepts a role/isAdmin field.

leads.title: [agent] Recycle records readable unauthenticated by ID (broken object-level authorization)

detail.text: GET /api/Recycles (collection) returns {"status":"success","data":{"err":"Sorry, this endpoint is not supported."}}, but GET /api/Recycles/1 and /api/Recycles/2 each return 200 with a ~206-byte JSON record with no session/Authorization. Recycle requests contain user address/quantity details, so individual records are exposed to anonymous callers by enumerating the numeric ID.

[agent] OPTIONS http://juice.lab.test/file-upload -> 204. Upload of unexpected file types could not be exercised directly (writes are disallowed; /file-upload only supports POST, OPTIONS shows GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE with wildcard CORS).
